title: Nth Digit
description: Brute force to optimized: building the digit sequence one number at a time versus skipping whole digit-length groups arithmetically.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given an integer n, return the nth digit of the infinite sequence formed by writing positive integers in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, and so on.

blocks.text: Concatenating every positive integer in order (1, 2, 3, ..., 9, 10, 11, ...) forms an infinite string of digits. Find the single digit sitting at position n in that string.

blocks.title: Analogy: Finding a Specific Character on an Infinitely Long Numbered Scroll
blocks.text: Picture an infinitely long scroll where someone has written out every counting number back to back with no spaces, 123456789101112..., and needing to find the exact character at a given position, without physically writing out billions of digits first.

blocks.caption: Numbers group by digit-length, each group contributing a known, countable number of digits

blocks.text: The sequence begins 1, 2, 3, ...; the 3rd digit is 3.
The sequence is 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,1,0,1,1,... (from 10, then 11); the 11th digit (1-indexed) is 0, the second digit of the number 10.
Before building the sequence character by character, notice that numbers group naturally by how many digits they have, and each group's total digit contribution is easy to compute directly.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: There are 9 one-digit numbers (1 through 9), contributing 9 times 1 equals 9 digits total; 90 two-digit numbers (10 through 99), contributing 90 times 2 equals 180 digits; and in general, 9 times 10 to the power (digits minus 1) numbers with that many digits.

Observation 2: Subtracting each group's total digit count from n, one group at a time, until n fits within the CURRENT group, identifies exactly which digit-length group the target digit falls into.

Observation 3: Once the correct group is found, dividing the (adjusted) remaining n by the digit-length identifies exactly which number within that group contains the target digit.

Observation 4: The remainder from that division identifies exactly which digit, within that specific number, is the answer.
This leads to arithmetically skipping whole digit-length groups, then directly computing the specific number and digit position within it.
Build the digit sequence one number at a time, appending its digits, until reaching position n.

items: Start building a string by appending "1", "2", "3", and so on.
Stop appending once the string's length reaches or exceeds n.
Return the character at position n minus 1 (0-indexed) in that string.

blocks.caption: Brute force flow: build the sequence one digit at a time until reaching position n

codes.python:
def find_nth_digit(n):
    digits = []
    num = 1
    while len(digits) < n:
        digits.extend(str(num))          # append this number's digits one at a time
        num += 1
    return digits[n - 1]

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Numbers are appended one at a time, in order, exactly matching the sequence's own definition.
The process continues until the built string is long enough to contain position n directly.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), potentially appending digits from roughly n divided by (average digit length) numbers.
Space: O(n), storing the entire built sequence up to position n.
Limitation: with n up to about 2 billion, both building and storing a sequence that long is completely impractical; the digit groups need to be skipped arithmetically instead.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why building the sequence is unnecessary: each digit-length group's total contribution (how many digits all its numbers add up to) can be computed directly, without listing a single number.

How to find the right group: subtract each group's total digit count from n, moving to longer digit-length groups, until n fits within the group currently being considered.

How to find the specific number: within that group, dividing the (by-now adjusted) n by the digit length identifies how many whole numbers into the group to skip.

How to find the specific digit: the remainder identifies exactly which digit within that specific number is the answer.

The core idea: skip entire digit-length groups arithmetically, then compute the exact number and digit position directly.

Track the current digit length (starting at 1), how many numbers exist at that length (starting at 9), and the first number at that length (starting at 1). While n exceeds the total digits contributed by the current length group, subtract that total from n and advance to the next length group. Once n fits within the current group, compute the exact number and digit index directly from n and the digit length.

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: skip whole digit-length groups, then compute the exact number and digit

codes.python:
def find_nth_digit(n):
    digits, count, start = 1, 9, 1
    while n > digits * count:                 # skip this whole digit-length group
        n -= digits * count
        digits += 1
        count *= 10
        start *= 10

    num = start + (n - 1) // digits             # the specific number containing the target digit
    idx = (n - 1) % digits                        # the specific digit within that number
    return str(num)[idx]

blocks.text: Each digit-length group contributes exactly (digit count) times (how many numbers have that many digits) digits in total, a value computable directly without listing any numbers. Subtracting these totals one group at a time correctly locates which group the target digit falls into; within that group, integer division and modulo directly locate the specific number and digit position, since every number in the group contributes the same, fixed number of digits.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(log n), since the number of digit-length groups grows logarithmically with n.
Space: O(1).

blocks.text: Nth Digit is a pure arithmetic problem once the sequence is understood as a series of digit-length groups, each with a directly computable size; no digit ever needs to be materialized before the exact one requested is located.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "n can be up to 2 billion, how do you avoid building the sequence", think: group numbers by digit length, and skip whole groups arithmetically.

Any problem involving grouping numbers by digit-length and computing group sizes directly, a common number-theory technique.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs in O(n) time and space. The optimized group-skipping approach runs in O(log n) time and O(1) space.

items: Pattern: grouping numbers by digit length, and skipping whole groups arithmetically.

Core Idea: each digit-length group contributes a directly computable number of digits; subtract group totals from n until landing in the right group, then compute the exact number and digit position with division and modulo.
Time: O(n) for the brute force, O(log n) for the optimized approach.
Space: O(n) for the brute force, O(1) for the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: every digit-length group's total digit contribution is computable directly, with no need to enumerate any numbers.
Interview Difficulty: the arithmetic is straightforward once the digit-grouping insight is recognized; careful indexing is the main pitfall.
One line memory trick: skip whole digit-length groups, then divide and mod to land on the exact digit.
